testSuite.name: Blog-QA Portfolio Business Process
testSuite.description: Comprehensive BDD test cases ensuring core blog, portfolio, and QA artifact functionalities operate as expected.

testCases.given: The user accesses the blog on a mobile device
testCases.when: The user taps the hamburger menu icon
testCases.then: The navigation menu expands and reveals page links

testCases.given: The application is currently in light mode
testCases.when: The user clicks the theme toggle button in the navigation bar
testCases.then: The UI switches to dark mode styling and the icon updates

testCases.given: The user is viewing the main Blog list page
testCases.when: The user clicks on a specific blog post title
testCases.then: The user is redirected to the blog detail page displaying the full article

testCases.given: The user is on the Contact page
testCases.when: The user fills in Name, Email, and Message fields and clicks 'Send'
testCases.then: The form clears and a success confirmation message is displayed

testCases.given: The user is on the Contact page
testCases.when: The user leaves the Email field empty and attempts to send
testCases.then: A validation error 'Email is required' appears

testCases.given: The user is on the Projects page viewing all projects
testCases.when: The user clicks on the 'React' technology tag
testCases.then: The project list updates to only display projects built with React

testCases.given: The user is viewing the 'Interactive Test Runner'
testCases.when: The user clicks the 'Pass' button for an idle test case
testCases.then: The test case highlights green and the execution progress bar increases

testCases.given: The user is interacting with the 'Bug Report Creator'
testCases.when: The user inputs severity, priority, and reproduction steps
testCases.then: A formatted JSON bug report payload preview is dynamically generated

testCases.given: The user navigates to the About page
testCases.when: The user scrolls to the technical skills section
testCases.then: Certifications (like the ISTQB badge) are rendered and visible

testCases.given: The user has the application open in their browser
testCases.when: Data is asynchronously added to the Firebase backend
testCases.then: The frontend automatically reflects the new data without requiring a manual refresh
